messages:
alex: CI started failing on flashattn_shared variant in the nightly build after the base image bump. linking errors like 'undefined reference to `cutlass::gemm`' and some PTX mismatches. anyone seen this?

maria: ugh saw a few failures too. only on ubuntu22 runners, mac and ubuntu20 green.

ci-bot: Build #1248 failed (eng-runtime/nightly-flashattn) — see /builds/1762001123/logs.

alex: paste of the linker tail:
```
/usr/bin/ld: /build/work/obj/libflashattn.a(flash_attn.o): in function `flash_attn::run':
flash_attn.cu:(.text+0x1a3b): undefined reference to `cutlass::gemm<float, ...>'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

sam: that looks like a cutlass ABI/inline namespace change. did the CUDA base image change? what’s the new image tag?

maria: CI image was bumped to nvidia/cuda:12.2-devel-ubuntu22.04 last week (was 12.1-ubuntu20.04).

sam: ok that explains it — some cutlass symbols get mangled when using a different gcc/clang combo. our build Dockerfile pins gcc-9 previously, debian/ubuntu22 default is gcc-11/12.

jen: Confirmed locally: building with system gcc12 produces the same link error. building with gcc9 (via update-alternatives) links fine.

alex: is the fix to pin gcc in CI or make our CMake handle symbol visibility? we can't keep downgrading toolchain forever.

maria: two parts: (1) many upstream kernels (cutlass/flashattn) assume a specific c++ abi and rely on -fno-common and some visibility flags. (2) nvcc host compiler integration changed slightly in 12.2 — host linker flags need tweaking.

sam: quick workaround: add these flags for host compile: `-fvisibility=hidden -fvisibility-inlines-hidden -D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1` and pass `-Xcompiler=-fno-plt`? not ideal.

ops: we should also reconcile the container toolchain with the release matrix. ops changed the base image to get new GPUs, but didn't pin the toolchain image. we can either pin gcc or update our third-party deps to be buildable under gcc12.

alex: unrelated but noticed perf regression in paged-attention benchmarks when fused kernels are selected for long sequence lengths. profiler shows increased L2 loads and stalling on shared memory. hypothesis: the fused kernel uses an extra transpose path that thrashes KV cache layout.

jen: saw that too — kv cache hit rate drops ~8% for seq_len=2048, batch=8 when fused kernel is selected. reverting to classic kernel restores hit rate and perf.

maria: patch idea: add a runtime guard in kernel selection to avoid fused variant when seq_len > 1024 or if KV working set > 1.2GB. cheap heuristic: if estimated KV pages > N then choose paged/fallback kernel.

sam: agree. Also for the build CI — propose triage steps:
1) reproduce locally in ubuntu22 container
2) run `nm` on libcutlass.a vs libcutlass built under gcc9 to diff symbol names
3) try forcing nvcc `--compiler-bindir` to gcc9 in the Dockerfile to see if that unblocks nightly

alex: I reproduced and attached logs (trimmed):
```
# in ubuntu22 container
docker run --rm -it nvidia/cuda:12.2-devel-ubuntu22.04 bash
apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential g++-9 g++-12 cmake
update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/gcc gcc /usr/bin/gcc-9 90
update-alternatives --set gcc /usr/bin/gcc-9
cmake .. -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc && make -j
```
Build passes with gcc-9 set, fails with default gcc-12.
```

ci-bot: New job queued to re-run with compiler-bindir override.

jen: For the longer term, we should document supported toolchains and adapt our packaging: publish prebuilt wheels or .deb for common combos, and update third-party submodules (cutlass) to their compat release branch.

ops: ops will pin the nightly image to the previous tag temporarily and add a blocker ticket to update infra docs.

maria: re: compile flags — there's also a floating point contraction difference: nvcc with gcc12 seems to enable `-ffp-contract=fast` in some cases which changes codegen for reduction kernels. add `-Xcompiler=-ffp-contract=off` to be safe for numerical determinism.

sam: thanks. Also spotted another CI-only failure: `thrust::system_error` thrown during unit tests while running on CI GPUs — stacktrace points to a missing PTX fallback path when compiling with `-gencode arch=compute_86,code=compute_86` vs sm_86 binary. switching to `code=sm_86,compute_86` fixed it local. probably nvcc flag semantics changed.

alex: action items we agreed on:
- ops: pin nightly image to last known-good tag (done quick PR).
- sam/maria: add a short-term CI change to pass `--compiler-bindir=/usr/bin/gcc-9` to nvcc and add `-Xcompiler=-fvisibility=hidden -Xcompiler=-fno-common -Xcompiler=-ffp-contract=off` for host builds.
- jen: add runtime guard in kernel selection to avoid fused kernel for large KV working sets. add unit test for KV hit rate sanity.
- alex: run full paged-attn perf sweep on the ubuntu22 image after CI change and report back.

ops: PR merged to pin image. re-running nightly now.

maria: quick perf note — when fused kernel is disabled for seq_len>=1536, the regression disappears with <3% drop vs baseline. we'll refine threshold after more runs.

alex: thanks everyone. leaving a few logs & a perf flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/graphs/1762001123. please 👍 on the CI flag PR if it unblocks you.

sam: gave PR a +1. we should also add a CI matrix job that runs gcc9 and gcc12 to catch these sooner.

jen: filed a small follow-up JIRA for kernel selection tuning (RT-4127).

ops: nightly passed after pin; will monitor next week. :relieved:
